metadata.description: open_bar: the bar imported and opened by the edge round on its own (offset in, re-distance, offset out), before the union - one block per bar slot.
The opened bars united as implicits (sharp). Bodies that cross each other come in separate bars: a mesh union's seams import as self-intersections. An unused slot repeats the smallest bar.
The bar (X radial, Y along the ring, Z axial) wrapped round the ring axis: one turn = Wrap Length.
The bar (X radial, Y along the ring, Z axial) wrapped round the ring axis: one turn = Wrap Length.

Spun about its own axis, a quarter-turn onto +X about the line through the pivot ∥ +Y, turned about the ring axis to its angle - in that order, one transform. An unused slot repeats the centre: the same head in the same place.
The pavé's beads on the shank (sharp: they are the pavé's own geometry). No pavé: a speck buried in the band.
The posts neighbouring stones share, and the bridge rails tying the heads together (Python's, in the ring frame; separate files so nTop unites them as implicits). Without: specks in the band.
The heads with the bridge and the posts (sharp: the bridge's section is each head's rail where they meet).
The heads melt into the shank (a smooth union). Every seat is cut AFTER it, the pavé's last: a blend fills every corner within its radius, the seats' included.
The text Python writes unwrapped, wrapped round the ring and turned under the finger, opposite the centre stone. Without text: a speck outside the ring.
The volume: ∫ 1 dV over the finished body (the notebook's Output; no density, no units).
